content.who_must_report: Public companies (those with publicly traded debt or equity)
content.management_approach: Segments based on how management internally organizes and evaluates the business (CODM - Chief Operating Decision Maker view)

three_characteristics: 1. Engages in business activities from which it earns revenues and incurs expenses
2. Operating results regularly reviewed by CODM for performance assessment and resource allocation

10_percent_tests.revenue_test: Segment revenue (including intersegment) ≥ 10% of combined revenue of all segments
10_percent_tests.profit_loss_test: Absolute value of segment profit/loss ≥ 10% of greater of: (a) combined profit of all profitable segments OR (b) combined loss of all loss segments
10_percent_tests.asset_test: Segment assets ≥ 10% of combined assets of all segments

quantitative_thresholds.reportable_if: Meets ANY ONE of the three 10% tests
quantitative_thresholds.75_percent_test: Reportable segments' external revenue must be ≥ 75% of total consolidated revenue. If not, identify additional segments until 75% threshold met.

aggregation_criteria.may_aggregate_if: Segments have similar economic characteristics AND similar in all of the following:
factors: If applicable, nature of regulatory environment

required_disclosures_per_segment: General information (factors used to identify segments, types of products/services)
Equity in net income of investees
reconciliations_required: Total segment revenues to consolidated revenues
Total segment profit/loss to consolidated income before tax
Total segment assets to consolidated assets

entity_wide_disclosures.revenues_by_product: Report revenues from external customers for each product/service or groups (even if not organized by product segments)
entity_wide_disclosures.revenues_by_geography: Report revenues from external customers: (a) domestic, (b) all foreign countries in total, (c) individual foreign countries if material
entity_wide_disclosures.major_customer_disclosure: If any single customer ≥ 10% of total revenues, disclose that fact, total revenues from such customer, and identity of segment(s)

calculation_example.75_percent_test: External revenue of reportable segments (A+B+C+D): $90+$80+$40+$30 = $240. $240/$255 = 94% > 75% ✓ → Sufficient reportable segments

cpa_exam_tips: Use TOTAL revenue (including intersegment) for revenue test
Profit/loss test uses ABSOLUTE VALUE and compares to GREATER of profitable or loss total
Don't forget reconciliations of segment totals to consolidated amounts
Major customer disclosure if ≥10% of entity's total revenue

calculation_steps: 1. Calculate combined totals (revenue, profit of profitable segments, loss of loss segments, assets)
3. Test each segment against ALL THREE 10% tests
4. Identify reportable segments (meet any one test)
5. Calculate external revenue percentage for 75% test
common_mistakes: Using external revenue only for revenue test (should include intersegment)
Comparing loss to wrong benchmark in profit/loss test
Forgetting absolute value in profit/loss test
Using internal revenue for 75% test (should be external only)

key_points: Operating segments based on management approach (CODM view)
Reportable if meets ANY ONE 10% test (revenue, profit/loss, assets)
Profit/loss test uses absolute value vs. greater of profit or loss total
75% test: reportable segments' external revenue ≥ 75% of total external revenue
Reconciliations required from segment totals to consolidated amounts
